description: Every way of addressing a Node builtin, and what each one comes to. Node's builtins are ambient `declare module` blocks inside `@types/node`, laid out here the way the real package lays them out — an entry point that is a hub of `/// <reference>` directives, so the walk that assigns package keys reaches no block and both package spellings fail, and differently. What reaches them is the `modules` table, keyed by the specifier of the block a declaration is *written* in: `path` colors `join`, while the same key under the `node:path` a reader actually imports is told which block to move it to. The whole report is named here rather than fragments of it, because the README quotes it and the docs gate holds the quotation to this.

names:
nothrow.overrides.json
  node:path → "." → `join`
    nothing of `node:path` is in this project, so there is no surface to hold this against. Inert rather than wrong.
  @types/node → "." → `join`
    `@types/node` publishes nothing at ".", and nothing at any other subpath.
    The walk from its entry points reached no name a carrier could key, so no entry under this package reaches anything.
  modules → "path" → `basename`
    "path" declares no symbol at this key, so this entry colors nothing.
    What it declares: `join`, `resolve`
  modules → "node:path" → `resolve`
    "node:path" publishes this key, and what it reaches is declared in "path" — which is the block a carrier is matched by, so this entry is never consulted.
    Key it under "path" instead.
  modules → "node:crypto" → `hash`
    nothing here declares the ambient module "node:crypto", so there is no surface to hold this against. Inert rather than wrong.
6 entries checked. 3 reach nothing; 1 names a package this project does not hold; 1 names an ambient module nothing here declares.
